notes: Forster resonance energy transfer efficiency within LHCII antenna to reaction center. >95% under normal conditions.

source_name: Jansson 1994 Biochim Biophys Acta; Croce & van Amerongen 2011 Nat Chem Biol
notes: Chl a/b ratio ~3:1 in most C3 plants. Higher Chl a in core complexes; Chl b in peripheral antenna.

source_name: Lavergne & Trissl 1995 Biophys J; Blankenship 2014
notes: ~200-300 Chl molecules per PSII reaction center depending on growth light conditions. Shade-adapted plants have larger antenna.

source_name: Maxwell & Johnson 2000 J Exp Bot
notes: Dark-adapted maximum quantum yield of PSII. Values >0.80 indicate healthy unstressed leaves. Stress reduces Fv/Fm.

source_name: Maxwell & Johnson 2000 J Exp Bot; Farquhar et al. 1980
notes: Maximum O2 evolution rate under saturating light at 25°C and 380 ppm CO2. Range 20-40 µmol O2 m-2 s-1.

source_name: Blankenship 2014 Molecular Mechanisms of Photosynthesis
notes: P680 excitation energy. Corresponds to ~680 nm absorption peak. Provides driving force for water oxidation (E0 +0.82 V vs NHE).

source_name: Blankenship 2014; Renger 2012 Biochim Biophys Acta
notes: Stoichiometry: 4 photons absorbed by PSII required per O2; 4 H+ released into lumen per 2 H2O split.

source_name: Cramer et al. 2011 Biochim Biophys Acta
notes: Cytochrome b6f turnover ~100-200 s-1 at 25°C. Rate-limiting step in linear electron flow under most conditions.

source_name: Allen 2003 Science; Cramer et al. 2011
notes: Q-cycle doubles proton pumping at cytochrome b6f: 2 H+ per electron passed through. Total 4 H+ per 2 electrons.

source_name: Kramer et al. 2004 Plant Cell Environ
notes: Proton motive force at steady-state illumination. ~70% from ΔpH component (~120 mV equivalent) ~30% from Δψ (~55 mV).

source_name: Klughammer & Schreiber 1994 Planta
notes: PSI quantum yield Y(I) at moderate light (~200 µmol photons m-2 s-1). Decreases at high light due to acceptor-side limitation.

source_name: Blankenship 2014 Molecular Mechanisms of Photosynthesis
notes: P700 excitation energy at ~700 nm absorption peak. Lower energy than P680 but sufficient to reduce ferredoxin (E0 -0.43 V).

source_name: Farquhar et al. 1980; Raines 2003 Photosynth Res
notes: Estimated from Calvin cycle demand. 2 NADPH per CO2 fixed × An ~5 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1 = 10 µmol NADPH m-2 s-1.

source_name: Allen 2003 Science
notes: Spinach CF1CF0 ATP synthase has 14 c-subunits per ring. 14 H+ per rotation / 3 catalytic sites = 4.67 H+ per ATP.

source_name: Allen 2003 Science; Raines 2003
notes: Linear electron flow produces ~1.28 ATP per NADPH. Calvin cycle requires 1.5 ATP per NADPH. Deficit supplemented by cyclic electron flow around PSI.

source_name: Kramer et al. 2004 Plant Cell Environ
notes: Stroma alkalinizes by ~0.5 pH units on illumination due to H+ pumping into lumen. Activates Calvin cycle enzymes (Rubisco activase etc).

source_name: Farquhar et al. 1980 Planta
notes: Representative An for sunlit C3 leaf under saturating light at 25°C ambient CO2. Range 15-25 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1.

source_name: Farquhar et al. 1980 Planta; Jordan & Ogren 1981
notes: Vo/Vc ~0.25 at 25°C 21% O2 380 ppm CO2. Increases with temperature. Represents ~25% carbon loss via photorespiration.

source_name: Farquhar et al. 1980; von Caemmerer 2000
notes: Michaelis constant for CO2 in chloroplast stroma. At ambient CO2 ~8-10 µM — near Km so Rubisco is substrate-limited.

source_name: von Caemmerer 2000 Biochemical Models of Leaf Photosynthesis
notes: Selectivity of Rubisco for CO2 vs O2. Sc/o ~80 in most C3 plants. Higher = less photorespiration. C4 plants circumvent via CO2 concentrating mechanism.

source_name: Raines 2003 Photosynth Res; Allen 2003
notes: Calvin cycle reduction stoichiometry: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH per CO2 fixed into G3P (net). Deficit in ATP/NADPH ratio from linear flow drives cyclic electron flow.

source_name: Raines 2003 Photosynth Res
notes: Stoichiometry of GAPDH reaction in Calvin cycle. 2 NADPH per 3-PGA reduced to G3P (per CO2 fixed net).

source_name: Stitt et al. 2010 Plant Cell Environ
notes: Estimated triose phosphate translocator flux at An ~20 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1. Roughly 1/5 of fixed carbon exported per turn of the cycle.

source_name: Stitt et al. 2010 Plant Cell Environ
notes: Net sucrose synthesis estimated from export rates and labeling studies. ~60-70% of fixed carbon exported as sucrose in mature spinach leaves.

source_name: Stitt et al. 2010 Plant Cell Environ
notes: Starch accumulates in the light at ~30-40% of fixed carbon. Remobilized nocturnally to maintain sucrose export. Stitt et al. 2010.

source_name: Stitt et al. 2010 Plant Cell Environ
notes: Approximately 65% of newly fixed carbon exported as sucrose; 35% as starch under well-lit conditions. Highly regulated by Pi and 3-PGA signals.
